day-1.t: Day 1 — What AI assistants can and cannot do

v: Know what an AI assistant is
See five jobs it does well
Know the three things it gets wrong

b.v: About 20 minutes. Open XpertCreation's AI Assistant (xpertcreation.com/assistant) in another tab and try each example.

An AI assistant is a program that has read a huge amount of text and learned how words usually follow each other. You type a request in normal language, and it writes an answer. It does not look things up in a book the way you do - it predicts a likely answer.

v: Writing a first draft: an email, a CV summary, a social media post
Explaining a hard topic in simple words, in Urdu or English
Summarising a long text into five points
Making lists and plans: a study timetable, a shopping list, an event plan
Rewriting: shorter, more polite, more formal, or for a child
Facts and numbers - it can invent a date, a law or a price that sounds right but is not
Very recent news - it may not know what happened this month
Your private situation - it does not know your company, your teacher or your family unless you tell it

b.v: Never copy an AI answer about medicine, law, money or religion and act on it without checking with a real expert or an official source.

Do this now:|Ask the assistant: Explain what inflation is to a 12-year-old, in 5 lines.|Then ask: Now say it in Urdu.|Then ask: Give one example from Pakistan.|Notice how each follow-up improves the answer.

day-2.t: Day 2 — How to ask: the 4-part prompt

v: Write requests that get useful answers the first time
Use the 4 parts: role, task, details, format

b.v: 1) Why short questions give weak answers
If you type only 'write a CV', the assistant has to guess your job, your experience and the style you want. It guesses something average. The more you tell it, the less it guesses.

v: Role - who should it act as? 'You are an HR manager in Lahore.'
Task - what exactly? 'Write a 4-line CV summary.'
Details - facts it must use: 'Accountant, 3 years, Excel, tax returns, looking for a bank job.'
Format - how should it look? 'Simple English, bullet points, no more than 60 words.'
Weak: Write an email to my boss.

Strong: You are my office assistant. Write a polite email to my manager, Mr. Ahmed, asking for leave on 12 and 13 December for my sister's wedding. I have finished the monthly report. Keep it under 80 words, formal English.

b.v: Keep a note on your phone with your best prompts. You will reuse them again and again.
Do this now:|Pick a real task you have this week.|Write it with all 4 parts.|Send it and compare with a one-line version of the same request.

day-3.t: Day 3 — Writing faster: emails, posts and CVs

v: Draft emails and posts in minutes
Improve your own writing instead of replacing it

b.v: Let the assistant write the first draft, then you change it so it sounds like you. Readers can often tell when a text is 100% AI: it is too long, too polite and full of words like 'delighted' and 'esteemed'.

v: Make this shorter and clearer: (paste your text)
Fix the grammar but keep my words
Write 3 versions: friendly, formal, very short
Turn these notes into a professional email: (paste notes)
Write a post for my bakery's page about our new chocolate cake, with 3 hashtags
Paste your job duties and ask: turn these into 5 achievement bullet points starting with action verbs
Ask: what skills is this job advert asking for? (paste the advert)
Never let it invent experience, degrees or numbers you do not have

b.v: A CV with invented facts can cost you the job when the employer checks. Use AI for wording, not for facts.
Do this now:|Write a 3-line message in your own words asking a shop for a price list.|Ask the assistant to make it polite and clear.|Change one sentence back to your own style.

v: Use AI as a tutor, not a cheat sheet
Make quizzes and flashcards from your notes

b.v: 1) Ask it to teach, not to answer

v: Explain photosynthesis step by step, then ask me 3 questions to check I understood
I think the answer is B because ... Am I right? Explain my mistake
Give me a simpler example of this formula
Paste your chapter notes and ask: make 10 multiple-choice questions with answers at the end
Ask: make 15 flashcards, question on one side, answer on the other
Ask: make a 7-day revision plan for these 5 topics, 1 hour a day

b.v: XpertAcademy's MCQ section and XpertCreation's own Assistant work well together: learn with the Assistant, then test yourself with real MCQs.
Many schools and universities count copying AI answers into homework as cheating. Use it to understand, then write in your own words.
Do this now:|Choose one topic from your studies or job.|Ask the assistant to explain it and then quiz you with 3 questions.|Answer them and ask it to mark your answers.

v: Spot invented facts
Check important answers in three quick ways

b.v: The assistant always produces an answer that sounds confident, even when it does not know. It can make up a book title, a court case, a phone number or a statistic. This is sometimes called a 'hallucination'.

v: Ask it: how sure are you, and what is your source? Then open the source yourself
Search the key fact on an official website (government, university, company page)
Ask the same question in a new chat - if the answers disagree, be careful
Exact numbers with no source
Very recent events
Laws, fees, tax rates and visa rules - they change often
Quotes from famous people

b.v: For tax, visa and fee questions, always end on the official website. The AI can tell you what to look for; the official page tells you the truth.
Do this now:|Ask: what is the fee for a new passport in Pakistan?|Then find the official passport office page and compare.|Write down which answer you would trust and why.

v: Describe a picture so AI can draw it
Know where AI pictures are fine to use and where they are not
Subject - a cup of chai on a wooden table
Setting - a balcony in the evening, city lights behind
Style - realistic photo / watercolour / flat cartoon
Details - steam rising, warm light, close-up
Format - square for a post, tall for a story
Ideas and mood boards before a real photo shoot
Backgrounds for posts and thumbnails
Illustrations for a lesson or a story
Make fake photos of real people, or put them in situations that never happened
Copy another company's logo or a famous cartoon character
Use an AI picture as 'proof' of a product you sell - customers expect the real thing

b.v: Fake pictures of real people can be against the law and can hurt someone badly. Do not make them, even as a joke.
Do this now:|Write a 5-part description for a poster of your favourite food.|Give it to an AI picture tool.|Change one part (style or light) and compare the two pictures.

v: Use AI for meetings, lists, spreadsheets and translations
Build a small daily routine
Turn rough meeting notes into minutes with action points and names
Write an Excel formula: 'I have dates in column A and amounts in B; total the amounts for March'
Translate a customer message from English to Urdu and back
Make a checklist for opening the shop every morning
XpertCreation's Video Translate turns a video into subtitles and a transcript in your language
Urdu voice typing turns your speech into written Urdu - then the assistant can polish it

b.v: Step by step:|Paste today's to-do list and ask: put these in order of importance and give each a time.|Paste unread customer messages and ask for short, polite reply drafts.|Ask for one tip to improve your work today.
Time yourself for one week. Most people save 3 to 5 hours on writing and planning alone.
Do this now:|Ask the assistant for an Excel formula for a real sheet you use.|Test it in Excel.|If it is wrong, tell the assistant what happened and ask again.

v: Know what never to type into an AI tool
Spot AI-made scams
Passwords, PINs and one-time codes
CNIC, passport and bank card numbers
Customer or patient details
Your company's secret documents, unless your company allows that tool
Voice calls that sound like a relative asking for money urgently
Perfect-English emails pretending to be your bank
Fake videos of famous people promising profits

b.v: If someone asks for money or a code in a hurry, stop. Call the person back on the number you already have, or visit the bank yourself.
Agree a secret word with your family. If someone calls claiming to be your son or sister in trouble, ask for the word. A scammer will not know it.
Do this now:|Agree a safe word with two family members today.|Check your phone for apps you gave AI access to, and remove any you do not use.

v: See small services you can sell
Price your work fairly and honestly
Writing product descriptions for small online shops
Turning a business's notes into social media posts for a month
Subtitles and translation for videos (Urdu, English, Punjabi)
CV and cover letter improvement
Simple presentations from a client's notes

b.v: Anyone can open an AI tool. Clients pay you for judgement: knowing what to ask, checking the facts, fixing the tone, and delivering on time. AI is your tool, the quality is your job.

v: Tell clients you use AI tools if they ask
Check every fact and name before you deliver
Never submit AI work as a student's own exam or thesis

b.v: You can offer these services on XpertCreation Freelance once your ID is verified.
Do this now:|Pick one service from the list.|Make one free sample for a friend's business.|Ask for honest feedback and improve it.
